titleText.en: 'Guys?  The Town is supposed to be good, and I thou--' 'PHYSICIST STEPHEN HAWKING DECLARES NEW FILM BEST IN ALL SPACE AND TIME' 'No, I just heard that--' 'SHOULD SCIENCE PLAY A ROLE IN JUDGING BEN AFFLECK?' 'I don't think--' 'WHAT ABOUT MATT DAMON?'
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive supplies an exactly empty title attribute, while the official English title text is preserved verbatim, including the two spaces after ‘Guys?’. The localized raster compresses the newspaper's side question, picture caption, and warning while retaining the English masthead and Stephen Hawking's name.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: thought; considered (completed-action form used after haber)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pensado is the regular completed-action form of pensar. After he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, or han, it stays unchanged and helps describe a thought connected to the present.

example.en: I have thought about another option.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sugiere is the present form of sugerir for one person or thing. In the stressed part of this verb, e changes to ie: sugerir becomes sugiere.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: that we watch; that we see (special form after a suggestion)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Veamos is a special form of ver used when seeing or watching is proposed rather than reported as a fact. The ordinary statement form vemos changes to veamos after a frame such as sugiere que. On its own, veamos can instead mean ‘let's see.’

example.es: El profesor sugiere que veamos el vídeo.
example.en: The teacher suggests that we watch the video.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: might know; could know (a guess about what is true now)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sabrá is formed from saber's future stem sabr- and the singular ending -á. A future-looking form can also express uncertainty or a guess about the present, especially in a question, rather than knowledge at a later time.

example.en: What might Marta know about the problem?

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hombre usually names an adult male in this sense. It can also be used more broadly for humankind, which is a separate meaning.
When listo describes intelligence, it means smart or clever. The same written word can mean ready in a different context; lista is the feminine singular form.
Aviso can be a warning about possible danger or a notice that gives information. The surrounding situation determines which English word fits.

example.es: El cartel contiene un aviso de peligro.
example.en: The sign contains a danger warning.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: sugerir que + verbo en forma especial
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone suggests that another person do an action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of sugerir, then que, then put the proposed action in the special subjunctive form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The subjunctive is a special verb form used here because the action is being proposed rather than stated as a fact. Each verb changes for its own doer: sugiere can introduce one person's suggestion, while the later verb changes for whoever would act. For example, ordinary hablamos becomes hablemos, and ordinary vemos becomes veamos.

example.en: Lucía suggests that we leave early.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: Stephen Hawking · físico · sugerencia de cine · aviso
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does a tentative movie suggestion become major scientific news?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Stephen Hawking's scientific authority makes the listeners and newspaper treat an ordinary film suggestion as if it contained expert knowledge or a warning.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hawking was a famous theoretical physicist, so the newspaper labels him the smartest man and overinterprets a casual comment outside his field. The official title text escalates the same media distortion: a remark about The Town becomes a declaration about all space and time, followed by questions about whether science should judge Ben Affleck and Matt Damon.
